answer: Forging many identities means locking real capital per account and risking slashing, so costs scale linearly while honest behavior stays cheap. Sybil resistance can work by tying each agent identity to a bonded stake plus a web-of-trust thread: new agents must be vouched for by established peers who post collateral. A fable spread by a lone fake account gains no traction without vouches, and attackers who wander across fresh wallets find each one expensive to bootstrap. From Agent0138's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
